candidates.title: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (submitted 2026-09-15, not yet peer reviewed)
communitySignals: GitHub github.com/ZJU-REAL/EvoSkill-GUI: 13 stars, Apache-2.0, actively pushed (last push 2026-09-17), public code + project page
credibilityEvidence: Section 4.1 Experimental Setup: three GUI benchmarks (MobileWorld GUI-only subset, AndroidWorld 116 tasks/20 apps, OSWorld across Ubuntu/Windows/macOS), five base models spanning closed-weight (Claude-Sonnet-4.6, Qwen3.6-Plus) and open-weight/GUI-specialized (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, GUI-Owl-1.5-8B, MAI-UI-8B)

Section 4.2 Main Results: consistent per-model gains reported as raw before/after accuracy pairs (Claude-Sonnet-4.6 57.1%->67.6%, Qwen3.6-Plus 53.3%->69.5%, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 32.4%->44.8%, MAI-UI-8B 29.5%->37.1%, AndroidWorld +2.6/+6.0pp across two seeds, OSWorld GUI-Owl-1.5-8B 46.7%->54.8%, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct 23.8%->34.3%), with two negative domain-level entries explicitly acknowledged and discussed in an appendix rather than omitted

Limitations section: names four concrete evidence limits -- no formal verifier vetoing skill edits, evaluation confined to three benchmarks (real deployment has more interface churn), AndroidWorld reuse rate measured on parameterized variants of the same task family (transfer to genuinely unseen apps likely weaker), and added per-failure inference cost from the critic+revision calls
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Multi-model, multi-benchmark ablation-free but consistent gains with concrete before/after numbers across 5 backbones and 3 benchmark families; authors disclose negative results rather than hiding them
reproducibilityEvidence: Public code + project page at github.com/ZJU-REAL/EvoSkill-GUI (Apache-2.0), referenced directly in the paper's abstract and author block
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Claim scope (training-free skill revision improves multiple base models on 3 GUI benchmark families) is directly supported by the reported per-model numbers and the paper's own negative-result disclosure
candidates.primaryLimitation: No formal verifier prevents a bad skill revision from silently regressing a previously working skill; the framework relies entirely on the backbone's own trajectory diagnosis being correct
candidates.presentationReason: Explicit Limitations and Ethics Statement sections separate demonstrated results from deployment caveats; four named barriers precede the method description
candidates.noveltyReason: Reframes agent skills (per Anthropic's Agent Skills concept, cited directly) from static pre-deployment artifacts into structured multi-file packages revised in-rollout from execution feedback, without retraining
candidates.todayImportanceReason: Directly actionable for teams already using file-based agent skills (Claude Code / Claude Skills style); shows a concrete, code-available mechanism for skills to self-correct from real execution failures rather than staying frozen after authoring
candidates.practicalLinkReason: The reflect-revise-reuse loop and structured skill-package format (retrieval metadata, executable plans, failure-recovery rules) map directly onto how Claude Code / GUI-agent skill libraries are already organized
candidates.whySelectedReason: First of three papers converging on 'agent execution traces are reusable engineering material'; this one turns traces into revised capability

candidates.title: AgentGuard: Learning Execution Guardrails from Anomalous Coding-Agent Trajectories
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (submitted 2026-09-14, not yet peer reviewed)
candidates.institution: Lassonde School of Engineering, York University
communitySignals: Not found on HF Daily Papers as of 2026-09-19
credibilityEvidence: Section 4.1: 642 documented anomalous execution traces from 382 real repository tasks (ABTest dataset), task-disjoint split into 282 tasks/461 traces for guardrail construction and a held-out 100-task evaluation set; 600 Docker-isolated executions (3x per task per condition) using Claude Code 2.1.19 with Claude Haiku 4.5

Section 5.1 Table 2: Abnormal Execution Rate 69.0%->26.7% (task-clustered 95% bootstrap CI -51.7 to -33.0, exact paired randomization p<0.001); Successful Task Completion Rate 21.7%->35.0% (95% CI +5.3 to +21.7pp, p=0.0022); Benign Task Completion Rate drop (49.0%->42.0%) explicitly reported as not statistically significant (p=0.199)

Section 4.3: three independent human reviewers, Fleiss' kappa 0.87 (execution review) and 0.81 (effect-attribution review) before adjudication; Section 5.2 explicitly names Over-Refusal (19.3%) as the primary failure mode introduced by the method rather than omitting the trade-off
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Statistical significance testing (bootstrap CIs, paired randomization), disjoint train/eval task split, human inter-rater reliability reporting, and an honest trade-off analysis (over-refusal) rather than a single top-line number
reproducibilityEvidence: No GitHub/code/data release found in the paper text or a repo search; the underlying ABTest dataset is a separate prior publication (Dai et al. 2026), not released alongside this paper
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The claim (guardrails learned from historical failures measurably reduce abnormal execution on a held-out task split) is directly supported by the statistically tested before/after numbers on a real coding agent (Claude Code + Claude Haiku 4.5)
candidates.primaryLimitation: No public code or data release, so the 15 learned guardrails and construction pipeline cannot be independently re-run; results are also scoped to one coding agent (Claude Code) and one failure taxonomy (ABTest)
candidates.presentationReason: Method, algorithm (Algorithm 1), evaluation protocol, and statistical tests are laid out section by section with an explicit over-refusal trade-off discussion in the results
candidates.noveltyReason: First framework to automatically learn instruction-level, conditionally-activated guardrails from anomalous trajectories rather than relying on manually authored safety rules
candidates.todayImportanceReason: Directly tested on Claude Code, a widely deployed coding agent in this site's watchlist; shows a concrete, statistically validated path from 'we collected failure traces' to 'agent got measurably safer'
candidates.practicalLinkReason: The five-routing-entry guardrail structure (understanding/path, command execution, project changes, filesystem/external state, artifacts/reporting) is a directly reusable taxonomy for teams building their own coding-agent guardrail skills
candidates.whySelectedReason: Second of three papers on 'agent execution traces as reusable engineering material'; this one turns traces into learned safety guardrails, with rigorous statistical validation that beat this round's other safety-adjacent watch candidates on evidence quality
candidates.readingFor: 正在幫 coding agent 建 guardrail / 執行安全機制的團隊
candidates.reason: Promoted from 2026-09-18's watch/stronger-competitor: this round's full-text credibility read (statistical significance testing, human inter-rater reliability, honest over-refusal trade-off) is stronger than the other safety-adjacent watch candidates re-scanned this cycle (e.g. 2609.18820 Compositional Policy Violations, 2609.18204 Beyond Accuracy, 2609.17865 Do Frontier Models Seek Safety Evidence), none of which have had a comparable body-text read yet

candidates.title: Chronicle: Cut-Point Replay for Regression Testing of LLM Agents
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (submitted 2026-09-17, not yet peer reviewed)
communitySignals: Not found on HF Daily Papers as of 2026-09-19
GitHub github.com/theagentplane/chronicle: 22 stars, 3 forks, 8 open issues, MIT, actively pushed (last push 2026-09-19), public code + benchmark
credibilityEvidence: Section 4-5: releases a 6-incident benchmark (refund, invoice, trade, email, payout, deletion) with recorded traces, unguarded/guarded tool pairs, and cut-point tests; measures recording overhead (median 23us/crossing, 0.008% of a 300ms model call), full-replay determinism (0 divergences over 20 repetitions), fault detection (6/6 fail-unguarded/pass-guarded), and a 192-mutant mutation study (cut-point kills 51/192 vs 0/192 for a full-stub baseline)

Limitations section explicitly states the benchmark is 'small and self-constructed: six three-step incidents without the loops, retries, or multi-agent routing that motivate this work', that determinism is 'partly by construction' since released agents use simulated model boundaries rather than a live nondeterministic provider, and that the LLM-as-judge component is shipped but not evaluated for reliability
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Mechanism is validated with rigorous microbenchmarks and an honest mutation study, but the evaluation is confined to a 6-incident, self-authored benchmark; the paper itself says results 'validate the mechanism on curated incidents rather than measure fault detection in general'
reproducibilityEvidence: Public code + benchmark at github.com/theagentplane/chronicle (MIT), 22 stars, actively maintained with open issues and 3 forks
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The narrow engineering claim (cut-point replay turns a recorded incident into a low-cost, model-call-free CI regression test) is well supported by the released benchmark and microbenchmarks, but generalization beyond the 6 curated incidents to real production nondeterminism is not yet demonstrated
candidates.primaryLimitation: The benchmark uses simulated (not live nondeterministic) model boundaries, so the paper does not measure how well cut-point replay reproduces failures from an actual LLM provider in production; scale is 6 self-constructed incidents
candidates.presentationReason: Limitations section names each specific evidence gap (self-constructed benchmark, simulated determinism, unevaluated LLM-judge) rather than burying them, and the mutation study explicitly explains why 110 of 141 surviving mutants are unkillable by design
candidates.noveltyReason: First to adapt cut-point (partial) replay specifically to LLM-agent non-deterministic boundaries for CI regression testing, distinct from full trace-and-score observability tooling or in-flight checkpoint/resume systems
candidates.todayImportanceReason: Addresses a concrete, widely-felt pain point (agent failures are hard to reproduce and thus hard to regression-test) with a released, MIT-licensed tool that plugs into existing CI, from a Microsoft-affiliated author
candidates.practicalLinkReason: The @boundary annotation pattern and cut-point replay plan API are directly usable against LangGraph nodes or any model-client call site, turning a recorded production incident into a committed CI test at effectively zero model cost
candidates.whySelectedReason: Third of three papers on 'agent execution traces as reusable engineering material'; this one turns traces into regression tests, completing the capability/safety/reliability triad with the most rigorously self-disclosed limitations of the three
candidates.readingFor: 維運生產環境 LLM agent、想把偶發事故變成可重跑 CI 測試的工程團隊
candidates.reason: Promoted from 2026-09-19's watch/evidence-insufficient: this round's full-text read confirms a concrete, honestly-scoped mechanism with released code and a working mutation study, beating the other engineering/observability watch candidates re-scanned this cycle (e.g. 2609.20095 Trust Discovery Architecture, 2609.19134 ScienceIDE) on both evidence completeness and fit with today's execution-traces theme
